newsitem.title: CHINA: China says first state asset registration finished.
newsitem.headline: China says first state asset registration finished.

text.p: China has completed its first national registration of the property rights of state adminstrative institutions, in a move aimed at curbing the loss of state assets, the China Daily newspaper said on Tuesday.
The registration process had revealed that some state enterprises did not list all their assets, while other lent or leased them in an uncontrolled way, the newspaper said.

The national registration, China's first, would help stem the loss of state assets and improve the way in which they were used, it quoted Pan Yue, deputy director of the State Administration of State Property, as saying.

Statistics showed that the 460,000 administrative institutions that were responsible for their own accounts held around 1,050 billion yuan ($126 billion) in assets, accounting for 18 percent of the state's total assets, China Daily said.
The registration aimed to clarify the assets of such firms, it said but gave no details.
